best_for: People with several email accounts who want mail, calendar and contacts in one free desktop app, with no ads in the inbox.
description:
Thunderbird is a free, open source email app that began in 2003 and is part of the Mozilla family. Its team works in a for-profit company owned by the nonprofit Mozilla, and a council elected by contributors helps set the budget and the roadmap. The project says it does not collect or store your personal data unless you ask it to.

You can set up filters that sort mail the way you like and change the look to suit how you work. If you want Thunderbird on your phone too, there is an Android app on Google Play and F-Droid. Anyone can help by testing new versions, reporting bugs, translating or writing code.

points.title: All your accounts in one inbox
points.text: Thunderbird handles email, calendar and contacts together. You can read every account in a unified inbox or keep them apart, and tag messages to find them later.

points.title: Free, funded by donations
points.text: It is open source under MPL-2.0 and paid for by user donations. Thunderbird says it does not sell inbox ads or train AI on your private mail.

points.title: Monthly releases are the default
points.text: Since version 136 the default download is the Release channel, with a new major version every month. The yearly ESR channel is still offered, and Thunderbird has advised add-on users to stay on ESR because some add-ons lag behind.

points.title: Windows 10 and macOS 10.15 or later
points.text: Version 160 needs Windows 10 or later, or macOS 10.15 or later on Intel or Apple Silicon. Windows 7 and 8.1 are left on the 115 ESR line. Linux builds are 64-bit only.

points.title: Flatpak from Mozilla
points.text: The Flathub build is verified as published by MZLA Technologies, part of Mozilla, and is x64 only. There is no Arm64 Flatpak here.

points.title: Deep history on Windows
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 139 versions in 32-bit and 64-bit, installed for all users. macOS and Linux list only the current release, so downgrades there need another source.
